author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Automatic game fixes simplify PCSX2 configuration
summary: PCSX2 moved compatibility knowledge into its GameDB so known corrections can be selected automatically instead of copied from scattered setup guides.
heroAlt: Automatic game fixes simplify PCSX2 configuration
searchKeywords: Automatic game fixes simplify PCSX2 configuration

blocks.text: From advice lists to executable knowledge

Older PCSX2 guides often told users to open separate CPU, speed-hack and graphics pages before launching one difficult title. The modern GameDB stores those verified requirements beside the game's serial and metadata, allowing the emulator to select known fixes before the VM starts.

A fix is associated with the identified game rather than with the user's whole installation. Regional releases and revisions can be distinguished when their executable behavior differs, preventing a correction tested on one build from becoming a global switch that silently changes unrelated software.

Graphics corrections such as native-scaling or half-pixel behavior can be activated for titles that exhibit the matching PS2 GS pattern. Users keep ordinary renderer defaults for the rest of the library, while maintainers can review the database entry and the code path that consumes it.

Automatic fixes do not replace per-game settings. GameDB entries represent compatibility knowledge maintained by the project; a user's preferred resolution, controller profile or memory card remains an explicit local override. Resetting personal settings therefore does not delete the project's known correction.

Starting from automatic defaults reduces configuration drift between testers. If a regression remains, a report can name the game serial, PCSX2 revision and active overrides instead of reconstructing a long forum checklist. The GameIndex source is versioned with the emulator, so changes can be reviewed and bisected. The per-game properties screen makes that ownership visible. Project-supplied compatibility rules remain distinct from the user's inherited and explicit choices, so troubleshooting can begin by clearing local overrides without discarding the database knowledge attached to the disc serial. Maintainers can then update one reviewed GameIndex entry instead of asking every user to repeat a fragile manual checklist.
